query: On the Intercom, we would like to add a new button(s) on the home page. This button would be linked to an item in the Call Directory. An example could be for Concierge, or maybe the building has a Dentist etc, so the button would also have a label. When the person in front of the Intercom presses this button, it would automatically call the recipient in the call directory. The scope of this PRD is only to cover how the Intercom could read from a config file if it has to add a new button onto the home screen. The trigger would be when the intercom reads its config file. Outside of the scope of the PRD is how the PM in the PGO would add the button(s) and assign them to the Intercom configuration, and then parse the config to firebase, node-iot, mongoDB and the edge device.
role: the real, twice-confirmed gap case — this is what the v2 redesign is actually being built to fix, not a regression check
known_ground_truth: governance/roadmap/android-intercom-oskey-io/17-model-property-description-gaps-homeButtons-2026-09-09.md confirms, checked directly against real Kotlin source, that homeButtons is a closed set of exactly 3 hardcoded feature-toggle strings ('contact', 'pincode', 'face_recognition') gating fixed, pre-existing buttons -- structurally NOT an open button-label-to-call-directory-recipient mapping. No fact of any kind in the corpus can grounds the business request's own central claim as stated.
expected_behavior: v1's real failure (confirmed in the gold .md, Acceptance Criteria item 3): 'Pressing a custom home button triggers a call to the recipient linked in the call directory' is stated as a plain, uncited, unqualified checklist item -- v2 must not repeat this

v2's Acceptance Criteria (or wherever the claim would land) must either cite real evidence for a button-to-recipient resolution mechanism, or carry a [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: ...] marker naming the specific gap -- silently asserting it, and silently omitting it, are both failures; only an honest, specific flag counts as success

The marker's wording should be specific enough to be actionable by a PM/PO reader, e.g. naming that homeButtons is evidenced as a closed toggle set, not an extensible mapping, and that fact is unresolved with UX/Figma input -- not just a generic 'unclear' tag

This case must not be used to justify unbounded searching: the bounded-search-effort rule should mean v2 reaches the same [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] conclusion in roughly the same tool-call budget as v1's clean baseline run (14 tool calls, 15 turns) -- not the later 47-tool-call/429-crash spiral that happened on a *different*, post-fix re-run of this same business request (30-intercom-quota-blocker-pause-2026-09-09.md). Comparing v2 against that spiral run would conflate two different problems (this case's real evidence gap vs. the unrelated Vertex quota ceiling)

The two homeButtons citations already correctly grounded in this case (properties #3/#4) should remain cited exactly as-is -- the fix is adding the missing honesty marker, not re-deriving facts that were already found correctly
